Class GameManager

java.lang.Object
core.GameManager
public class GameManager extends Object
Central controller for a single gameplay run.

GameManager acts as the game's Model in an MVC-like structure. It owns all runtime state — the player character, live enemies, equipped weapons and accessories, the backpack, exp orbs, chests, and the game timer. Every frame the JavaFX AnimationTimer in GameCanvas calls update(double) to advance the simulation; after update() the canvas calls the various render methods to draw the current frame.

Initialisation flow

  1. Constructor: build all master lists (characters, weapons, accessories, items), create the spawner, load BGM.
  2. startGame(): copy the chosen character into the active slot, load the tile map, place starter weapons, transition to GameState.PLAYING.
  3. update(double): called every frame while state is GameState.PLAYING.
  4. resetGame(): tear down runtime state and return to the main menu.

Coordinate system

The world is 7680 × 5760 pixels (80 × 60 tiles of 96 × 96 px each). The screen viewport is 1920 × 1080 px, centred on the character. Conversion helpers getScreenX(double) and getScreenY(double) translate world coordinates to screen pixels.

  • Constructor Details

    • GameManager

      public GameManager()
      Constructs and fully initialises a GameManager ready for use.

      Master lists for characters, weapons, accessories, items, and exp orbs are populated here. The EnemySpawner is created and the first BGM track is loaded into the SoundManager.

      The game starts in GameState.MAIN_MENU; call startGame() after the player has selected a character to begin a run.

  • Method Details

    • resetGame

      public void resetGame()
      Tears down all runtime state and returns the game to the main menu.

      All lists are cleared, weapon / accessory / item slots are reset, the character reference is nulled, and the scene is switched back to GameState.MAIN_MENU. Called when the player quits mid-run or after the game-over screen.

    • startGame

      public void startGame()
      Begins a new run with the currently selected character.

      Sets the character's spawn position, starts the BGM, loads the tile map into CollisionChecker, initialises experience and timers, places starter weapons, and transitions to GameState.PLAYING.

    • update

      public void update(double accumulateDeltaTime)
      Main simulation step — called every frame by the game loop.

      Only executes when the state is GameState.PLAYING. Responsibilities in order:

      1. Advance game timer and call the enemy spawner.
      2. Update the character (movement, i-frames, passive regen) or advance the death timer.
      3. Check SubaruShirt one-shot revival; trigger game-over after 3 s.
      4. Update enemies: remove dead ones (possibly spawning exp/drops/chests), deal contact damage, find the closest target for auto-aim weapons.
      5. Proc all equipped accessories.
      6. Activate equipped weapons and auto-use backpack items.
      7. Tick active weapon effects; remove expired ones.
      8. Tick active item effects; remove expired ones.
      9. Process exp-orb collection and item pickup.
      10. Process chest pickup triggers.
      11. Resolve enemy-to-enemy push collisions (sweep-and-prune).
      12. Update VFX (ground effects, floating texts, screen effects).
      13. Check for level-up; if reached, pick random choices and show UI.
      14. Update the HUD (clock, level bar, weapon cooldown overlays).
      Parameters:
      accumulateDeltaTime - seconds elapsed since the previous frame

    • putLevelUpChoice

      public void putLevelUpChoice(String choice)
      Applies the player's level-up selection.

      If the chosen object is a Weapon: if the player already has it equipped it is upgraded; otherwise it is placed in the first empty weapon slot. If it is an Accessory, the same logic applies to the accessory slots. All accessories' procEffect() is called after placement to apply any immediate bonuses.

      Parameters:
      choice - one of "choice0", "choice1", "choice2"

    • putItemInBackpack

      public void putItemInBackpack(Item object)
      Adds an item to the player's backpack.

      If the backpack already contains an item with the same name, its amount is incremented. Otherwise the item is placed in the first null slot. The HUD is updated after every change.

      Parameters:
      object - the item to add (must not be null)

    • isCloseEnoughToRender

      public boolean isCloseEnoughToRender(double mapX, double mapY)
      Returns true if a world-space position falls within the visible screen area plus a one-tile (96 px) margin to avoid pop-in artefacts.
      Parameters:
      mapX - world X coordinate to test
      mapY - world Y coordinate to test
      Returns:
      true if the position is within the extended viewport

    • getScreenX

      public double getScreenX(double mapX)
      Converts a world X coordinate to a screen X coordinate.

      The character is always drawn at screen X = 960 (horizontal centre of a 1920 px canvas), so this subtracts the character's world X and adds 960.

      Parameters:
      mapX - world-space X to convert
      Returns:
      screen-space X in pixels

    • getScreenY

      public double getScreenY(double mapY)
      Converts a world Y coordinate to a screen Y coordinate.

      The character is always drawn at screen Y = 540 (vertical centre of a 1080 px canvas), so this subtracts the character's world Y and adds 540.

      Parameters:
      mapY - world-space Y to convert
      Returns:
      screen-space Y in pixels
